results.rationale: Both implement an online regime-aware portfolio of restart policies mixing Luby-like, LBD-drift, and stagnation triggers with extra diversification actions, but B uses a fixed regime-to-policy mapping plus PAR2/risk-based global scaling and cooldown whereas A uses UCB bandit selection among more policies and richer multi-signal scoring.

Both implement a portfolio of restart modes (Luby/geom plus adaptive LBD/trail/progress triggers) selected online by a bandit with rewards from LBD/propagation/progress metrics, differing mainly in bandit type (UCB+change-point per-restart vs Exp3 per-epoch) and specific trigger details.

Both are adaptive multi-signal restart controllers using LBD/glue/trail/backjump/propagation-style signals and post-restart feedback, but A is a bandit-selected portfolio of distinct restart policies with diversification actions, while B is a single weighted pressure score plus dynamic budget and soft-vs-hard restart logic.

Both are adaptive multi-signal restart governors that classify search regime and choose between soft/hard restarts while scaling restart frequency based on LBD/progress/slowdown signals, but they differ in controller form (A uses a single weighted pressure+dynamic budget with reward-tuned threshold, B uses a discrete 3-policy portfolio with PAR2 risk scaling and Luby/Glucose-like sub-schedulers).

Both replace a single restart rule with an Exp3-selected portfolio of restart modes/policies driven by conflict-index scheduling plus adaptive triggers from EWMAs (e.g., LBD/stagnation/progress), differing mainly in B’s per-restart policy reselection and extra phase-aware overrides versus A’s epoch-fixed mode and different trigger set (agility/trail vs stagnation sigmoid/instability).

Both implement a portfolio of restart modes/policies chosen online by a bandit using per-restart rewards from LBD/propagation-style signals plus a temporary NoRestart option, differing mainly in bandit type (UCB1+CUSUM vs Exp3+phase overrides) and the exact trigger/signal formulas.

Both implement an online-selected portfolio of restart schedules using bandit learning over conflict/LBD/trail/backjump/speed-style signals with additional hard override/gating rules, differing mainly in bandit type (UCB1 vs Exp3), exact health metrics, and policy set (A has explicit OR-gates and four modes; B has policy-specific triggers plus a NoRestart option).

Both implement an adaptive portfolio of multiple restart modes (Luby/geometric plus special no-restart/stagnation-like behaviors) selected online via bandit-style reward updates from LBD/trail/progress signals, differing mainly in the bandit controller (UCB+changepoint vs softmax/EXP3 with extra stability gating and burst mode).

Both are adaptive multi-signal restart controllers using EMAs for stagnation/instability/slowdown and adding phase perturbations on “stuck” conditions, but A’s core is a bandit-selected portfolio of restart schedules with hard OR-gates while B uses a single weighted restart-pressure threshold plus a multiplicatively adapted budget and explicit soft-vs-hard restart classification.

Both replace a single restart schedule with a bandit-controlled portfolio of multiple restart modes (including Luby/geometric and stagnation-based triggers) using progress signals like LBD/trail to reward and reweight modes, differing mainly in B’s extra modes and stabilization gating/softmax update details.

Both use an online UCB1 bandit to select among multiple restart schedules (e.g., Luby/geom plus adaptive modes) based on per-period rewards from LBD/core-clause and search-efficiency signals, differing mainly in B’s explicit health-gate triggers and A’s richer phase/decay band definitions.

Both are multi-policy restart portfolios using Luby/geometric-style schedules plus LBD/stagnation/propagation signals, but A selects modes via bandit learning over epochs while B uses per-conflict regime classification with risk-scaled intervals and adds phase-reset hard restarts.

Both are adaptive restart schemes driven by online LBD/trail/backjump-style signals, but A uses a single weighted unproductivity threshold with soft/hard restart actions while B uses a bandit-selected portfolio of restart schedules with reward-based policy switching and overrides.

Both are adaptive, health-signal-driven restart schemes using EMAs of LBD/trail/stagnation to gate restarts, but A is a single weighted unproductivity controller with soft/hard restart actions while B is a portfolio/bandit selector over multiple restart schedules with separate gate logic and mode switching.

Both are adaptive, multi-signal restart schemes using LBD/trail/propagation/stagnation-style signals and occasional hard restarts, but A is a single weighted unproductivity-threshold controller with budget multiplier while B is a regime-classifier that switches among distinct policies (Luby/Glucose/aggressive) and adds a time-based PAR2 risk scaler and cooldown.

Both are adaptive restart schemes using online LBD/trail/propagation signals and stagnation/panic-style early restarts, but A is a single weighted unproductivity-threshold controller with soft/hard restart actions while B is a multi-mode portfolio chosen by a UCB bandit with change-point resets and mode-specific schedules.

Both are adaptive restart schemes driven by overlapping online signals (LBD/glue rate, trail depth, propagation/backjump/stagnation) and include diversification actions, but A uses a single weighted unproductivity score with dynamic budget and soft/hard restart types while B uses a portfolio of distinct trigger rules with bandit (UCB1) selection and regime-based phase/activity switching.

Both are adaptive restart schemes using EMA-style progress signals (notably LBD/trail/propagation/stagnation), but A is a single weighted unproductivity controller with soft/hard restart actions and dynamic budget, while B is a portfolio of distinct schedules/triggers chosen by an Exp3 bandit with mode-level switching.

Both are adaptive restart controllers using multiple progress signals (LBD/trail/stagnation) to modulate restart aggressiveness, but A is a single weighted unproductivity-threshold with soft/hard actions while B is a bandit mixture over discrete schedule modes with reward-based probability updates and windowed triggers.

Both are adaptive restart schemes driven by online LBD/progress/propagation-style signals and include soft-vs-hard/phase diversification, but A’s core is a UCB multi-band scheduler over distinct restart policies while B is a single weighted unproductivity controller with dynamic budget/threshold logic.
